items.note: Fetched city press release (published 29 Apr 2025, in force 1 Jun 2025). Confirms replaces 2008 ordinance, five zones, higher fees in Altstadtinsel and Travemünde while peripheral lots stay cheaper, 30-minute steps instead of per-minute billing, Broetchentaste 10 to 15 min, EV free parking initially to end of 2026, short-notice adjustment at major events. Date 2025-06 is the effective date (publication was April 2025). Overlaps with item 1 (same source); could be merged.

Same city press release as item 0; tariff table matches exactly: Zone I 1.50/3.00/no day ticket, Zone II 1.20/2.40/8.00 (ring around Altstadt incl. Kanalstraße), Zone III 1.00/2.00/6.00, Zone IV 1.60/3.20/12.00, Zone V 1.20/2.40/no day ticket; motorhome EUR 20 per 24 h and coach EUR 30 per day confirmed. Duplicate source with item 0 (merge candidate). Also confirmed by the ordinance PDF (item 2).

Downloaded ordinance PDF and read it. Par. 1 says public parking areas are managed by KWL GmbH; Par. 2 lists Zone IV lots exactly as stated (incl. Backbord, Hafenbahnhof, Am Fischereihafen); Par. 9 EV free parking to 31 Dec 2026 on all fee-paying spaces except Zones I and IV (the ordinance specifies 'im öffentlichen Straßenraum'). Day-ticket annex shows Zone I has no day ticket. Supported.

hl-live article of 22 May 2025 confirms: CDU, Grüne and FDP (described as a majority) want the Kommunalaufsicht to check whether the mayor may raise fees without Bürgerschaft consent; mayor rejected changes and presented a six-page legal opinion from the Rechtsamt; critics say inner city becomes less attractive for car customers; Altstadt EUR 3 per hour and day ticket abolished from 1 June. Wording 'moved to ask' is slightly stronger than 'want to' but acceptable. Local press source (HL-live).

hl-live article of 10 Sep 2024 confirms EUR 1.20/h or max EUR 4/day in Travemünde, just under EUR 800,000 for the Kurbetrieb in 2023, aim to raise the day maximum at Leuchtenfeld, Möwenstein, Backbord from 4 to 6 (Wirtschaftsplan 2024) and the Kurbetrieb's proposal of EUR 8; about EUR 6 million collected in the previous year and EUR 6.6 million planned for the coming year. Background only, superseded by the 2025 ordinance; low value.

City press release published 7 Aug 2026: 'Es ist geplant' to raise permits from EUR 30.70 to EUR 90 a year from 1 Sep 2026; state ordinance early 2026 allows up to EUR 90; Bürgerschaft had recommended it; cost recovery and limited street space as reasons. Item correctly words it as a plan. It is superseded by item 6 (decided ordinance, in force 1 Sep 2026): overlap, merge into item 6 or drop 5.

Downloaded PDF and read it: BePVO, signed Lübeck 28.08.2026, Par. 3 fee EUR 90.00 per year of validity, validity 1-3 years, Par. 5 in force 1.9.2026. Title matches the PDF heading. Supported; this is the decided version of item 5 (permits rising from EUR 30.70 comes from item 5's source, not this PDF).

Draft URL (.../verkehrsentwick-lungs-plan/index.html) resolves to the city's Verkehrsentwicklungsplan page. Confirms June 2022 Bürgerschaft guidelines, modal split Umweltverbund 56% (2017) to 70% (2040), MIV 44% to 30%, and that the administration planned to circulate the VEP decision paper in Q3 2026. The page is undated and the status text looks stale (written in 2025), so the Q3 2026 statement is a plan whose outcome we have not verified. Peripheral to parking; low value.

City project page confirms first construction phase of upper Beckergrube (Breite Straße to Kupferschmiedestraße/Fünfhausen) began October 2024, due to finish autumn 2026, EUR 3.5 million from federal programme 'Nationale Projekte des Städtebaus', part of 2019 Rahmenplan Innenstadt mit Mobilitätskonzept. Page's own press list (4 Aug 2026) says completion planned for end of November 2026, so still a plan as of today; page is a live page.

hl-live article dated 25 May 2026 confirms closed to cars since 9 Feb 2023, pedestrian bridge lifted out Nov 2024, road and rail bridges' Aushub planned for 2026, estimated EUR 40 million, main works depend on federal budget funds. Item date 2023-02 is the closure date; the article itself is from May 2026 (use 2026-05 if the date should be the source date).

hl-live (Presseamt/VG) article of 5 Dec 2025 confirms closure after inspection rated 4.0 (ungenügend), described as important access from the south, 'after the Hubbrücke', detour via Berliner Platz, Possehlstraße and Wallstraße from 5 December, pedestrians and cyclists can use the temporary bridge. Supported.

hl-live article of 11 Dec 2025 confirms Burgtor/Große Burgstraße access banned 10:30-22:00 daily (city cites stronger protection measures for the Christmas market; article says the actual reason stays unclear), speed-camera trailer, EUR 50 fine, and the city statement that KOD tightened checks on Rippenstraße and Große Burgstraße also to stop growing parking-search traffic by unauthorised drivers. Supported.
City service page says 'In Lübeck gibt es keine Umweltzonen in denen eine Umweltplakette benötigt wird.' Page is undated (read 2026). Very low value for a parking briefing; candidate to drop.

Homepage of parken-luebeck.de (live page, undated, read 7 Oct 2026; all capacities match): Am Fischereihafen 393, Backbord 135, Hafenbahnhof 46, Kanalstraße P3 122, P4 145, P5 46, Kowitzberg 450, Lastadie P5 250, MuK 350, Radisson Blu 61. But 'more than 70 car parks and garages ... with live free-space counts' is overstated: the page lists 76 entries of which only 48 are car parks, 6 kerbside areas and 10 garages (the rest are motorhome bays, permit-only spaces and a charging point), and only about 20 show live counts (the rest say 'Keine Live-Daten verfügbar'). The homepage itself does not call KWL the city's company (items 2 and 3 do: KWL manages the public parking areas). Capacity differences with our feed are not explained by the page.
items.corrected_text: KWL GmbH, which the city's fee ordinance names as manager of Lübeck's public parking areas, runs the parking site parken-luebeck.de. In October 2026 the site listed 76 parking locations in Lübeck and Travemünde (car parks, garages, kerbside areas, motorhome bays and permit spaces), only some with live free-space counts. Listed capacities of the measured car parks: Am Fischereihafen 393, Backbord 135, Hafenbahnhof 46, Kanalstraße P3 122, Kanalstraße P4 145, Kanalstraße P5 46, Kowitzberg 450, Lastadie P5 250, MuK 350, Radisson Blu 61 (undated live page, read in October 2026).

items.note: MuK page on parken-luebeck.de (title 'MuK | KWL GmbH'; live undated page, read 7 Oct 2026): 350 spaces ('Parkplaetze gesamt: 350'), Willy-Brandt-Allee, open 24 h, fee Mo-Sa 10-18, 1.20 per 30 min, 2.40 per hour, 8.00 per day, 'Kostenloses Parken für E-Autos'. Matches. Tariff is consistent with Zone II in the ordinance, but the ordinance text does not name MuK, so the zone assignment is not independently confirmed. Undated, medium confidence is right.

Draft URL redirects (308) to apcoa.de/en/park-once/locations/luebeck/linden-arcaden; page title 'Linden Arcaden - APCOA'. Confirms off-street underground, Konrad-Adenauer-Straße 2, 23558 Lübeck, 456 spaces, open 00:00-00:00 every day; KWL homepage also lists 'Linden Arcaden - Parkhaus'. Page is a live, undated listing (and APCOA tariff from EUR 2.60/h, max EUR 25/day was not used). Low analytical value but accurate.

hl-live article of 28 Mar 2025 (KWL/red.) confirms opening on 28 March 2025, seven levels, 301 spaces, ten EV charging points, camera plate recognition without barriers, EUR 2.00/h, EUR 8.00/day, EUR 79/month and planned connection to the parking guidance system. Errors: (1) the EUR 79 is for 'Dauermieter' (long-term renters), not 'permit holders'; (2) 'built by KWL' is wrong: KWL implemented it on behalf of the city and it was built by the general contractor Deutsche Industrie- und Parkhausbau GmbH; (3) the street 'Am Fahrenberg' is not in this article (it appears in the Travemünder Woche notice, item 23's source). Also note the July 2026 KWL notice (item 23) gives Godewind as 253 spaces, versus 301 here.
items.corrected_text: The Parkhaus Godewind in Travemünde was officially opened on 28 March 2025: seven levels, 301 spaces, ten EV charging points, barrier-free operation via camera number-plate recognition, EUR 2.00 per hour or EUR 8.00 per day, EUR 79 per month for long-term renters, and a planned connection to the city's parking guidance system. It was implemented by KWL on behalf of the city and built by Deutsche Industrie- und Parkhausbau GmbH.

items.note: hl-live article of 17 Mar 2026 (reply by the city administration to a Grüne inquiry): monthly utilisation between 6.7% (April 2025) and 16.7% (July), peak 90% at 22:42 on 27 July 2025 (Travemünder Woche), 14,150 motorists by year-end, 2025 loss EUR 640,821.95 of which Lübeck indirectly bears 80%. All as stated. The 11.6% in the headline appears only in the headline; the article body never defines what it measures (period, hours), so do not cite the 11.6% figure as a utilisation number; the draft text correctly omits it. Article notes the garage is open 24 h, which depresses average utilisation.

hl-live article of 25 Sep 2025 (KWL/red.): after partial reopening for permit renters about six months earlier, fully open also to short-stay parkers; over EUR 4 million invested; chloride-induced corrosion; 316 spaces; barrier-free with card and phone payment; online shop with weekly tickets; seven charging points with Stadtwerke Lübeck plus two further charging posts (three points) reserved for StattAuto car sharing. Supported. Low demand relevance.

hl-live article of 25 Oct 2025 (KWL/red.) confirms the text (closure 'bis auf Weiteres' effective 31 Dec 2025, structural problems found seven years earlier, only temporary operating permits after load tests, Bürgerschaft 2019 decision to build a new garage on the same site). The announcement was made on 25 October 2025, so the item date should be 2025-10, not 2025-12 (the closure date). The article also says implementation of a new building was 'not certain' at that time, later superseded by item 20.
items.corrected_text: KWL announced on 25 October 2025 that the Parkhaus Am Holstentor would be closed until further notice from 31 December 2025, because continued operation without extensive investigation was no longer possible; structural problems had been found seven years earlier and operation had been extended only temporarily after load tests. The Bürgerschaft had decided in 2019 to build a new garage at the same site.

items.note: hl-live article of 5 Jun 2026 (KWL/red.): demolition planned for coming months (contract awarded), estimated 5-7 months, about EUR 1.5 million; competition winner dip GmbH with Schmieder Dau Architekten; building application to be submitted in August, construction start planned Q1 2027, completion expected Q3 2028, construction costs expected about EUR 13.2 million. All stated as planned in the draft. Supported (the rebuild is a plan; not verified that the building application was in fact filed).

hl-live article of 1 Apr 2025 (KWL/red.) is an announcement in the future tense ('wird ... kosten'): the Parkhaus is closed for short-stay parkers on 8 and 9 April for the new payment system, card payment added, app payment planned from summer, price EUR 2.50/h and EUR 12.50/day, previously EUR 1.50/h and EUR 7.50/day. The draft says the price 'rose'; the source only announces the increase. The garage has been closed since 31 Dec 2025 (item 19), so the tariff is of low current value.
items.corrected_text: KWL announced on 1 April 2025 that the payment system at Parkhaus Holstentor would be modernised (card payment added, app payment planned from summer) and that the price would rise from EUR 1.50 per hour and EUR 7.50 per day to EUR 2.50 per hour and EUR 12.50 per day.

items.note: hl-live article of 14 Aug 2025 (Presseamt Lübeck/red.): P1 on Kanalstraße to be closed to the public from Monday 1 September 2025 for an interim modular school (36 modules, up to 420 pupils from August 2026), expected five years (later used as interim space until about 2031); city says the lot is 'nicht hoch frequentiert' and sufficient parking is available nearby. The article is written before the closure ('wird gesperrt'); that P1 is indeed closed is consistent with KWL's current list, which shows only Kanalstraße P2-P5. Supported.

hl-live (KWL/red.) of 16 Jul 2026: 137th Travemünder Woche 17-26 Jul 2026; Am Fischereihafen 400 spaces (the KWL list shows 393), Backbord 135 spaces, both EUR 1.60/30 min, EUR 3.20/h, EUR 12 day ticket, 10-18 h; Kowitzberg free lot (15-20 min walk, no capacity or 'overflow' wording in this article); Leuchtenfeld about 300 of 750 spaces public, EUR 3.00/h, no day ticket, charged 10-22 h; Möwenstein closed by the organiser. The article also lists Godewind with 253 spaces (versus 301 in item 16), which is a discrepancy worth noting. Supported.

hl-live (Presseamt/red.) of 4 Dec 2025: city recommends bus and rail, free shuttle on Advent Saturdays every 10 min from P+R Lohmühle and Einsiedelstraße, 11:05-20:35, LED signs on approach roads direct drivers to the P+R lots, inner-city parking limited and drivers urged to follow the parking guidance system. Supported. Low parking-demand value (event communication).

Downloaded PDF (Frage-Antwort-Protokoll Travemünde 08.01.2026, file 'fragenkatalog_stadtteilkonferenz_travemuende_08.01.2026'): answer to Q29 says a Parkraumkonzept for Travemünde is being prepared, among other things to answer how parking-search traffic can be reduced; Q34 says the dynamic signage with live data for Parkhaus Godewind will be finished before the main season (data link expected in February). Both framed as plans in the draft. Supported.

hl-live (WiFö HL/VG) of 14 Sep 2026 on Einzelhandelsmonitor 2026 (Stichtag 31 Dec 2025): inner-city sales EUR 252.9 million in 2025 vs EUR 294.4 million in 2024, inner-city vacancy rate 20.5%, postcode 23556 (CITTI, Rewe-Center) EUR 280.6 million, higher than the inner city. Supported. The source attributes the decline to weak consumer sentiment, energy prices and inflation, not parking; relevance to parking is indirect, so this is one of the weaker items.

KWL E-Mobilität page (live, undated): E-plate vehicles park free under the EmoG on listed lots incl. Kanalstraße, Lastadie (also P2 and P4 Womo), MuK, Wallstraße, Müllergarten; 'Die Regelung zum kostenlosen Parken für E-Autos endet 2026'; blue charging sign: free up to 3 hours while charging (2 h at fast chargers; the page adds 8-20 h and excludes private garages). Matches; duplicates the EV point in items 0 and 2 (merge candidate).

corrected_summary: Lübeck's public car parks and on-street fees are managed by the city company KWL GmbH under a fee ordinance in force since 1 June 2025, which charges EUR 3.00 per hour with no day ticket in the Altstadt and EUR 3.20 per hour (EUR 12 day ticket) in Travemünde's centre; residents' permits rose from EUR 30.70 to EUR 90 a year on 1 September 2026. Altstadt access is constrained by the Hubbrücke (closed to cars since February 2023), the Mühlentorbrücke (closed on 5 December 2025), the Beckergrube redesign (first phase due to finish in autumn 2026) and Christmas-market access restrictions, while the Parkhaus Am Holstentor has been closed since 31 December 2025 and KWL plans to demolish it and open a replacement in about the third quarter of 2028. In Travemünde the new Parkhaus Godewind was lightly used in 2025 (monthly utilisation between 6.7% and 16.7%, a loss of EUR 640,821.95), and Kanalstraße P1 in Lübeck was closed on 1 September 2025 for a school building expected to stand for about five years. Inner-city retail sales fell from EUR 294.4 million in 2024 to EUR 252.9 million in 2025, while the CITTI postcode area reported EUR 280.6 million.
